title: Leaders, Anger, and Honest Living
overview: This chapter collects short sayings about how character, especially the character of rulers, shapes families, courts, and whole nations.

parts.label: Stubbornness and rulers (vv. 1-4)
parts.note: Someone who keeps refusing correction will one day collapse with no way back. A whole country feels its leaders' character: fair rulers bring joy and stability, while rulers greedy for bribes tear the land apart.

parts.label: Traps and troublemakers (vv. 5-11)
parts.note: Flattery sets a trap, either for the person praised or for the flatterer, and wrongdoing snares the one who does it. Mockers stir a city into conflict and a fool in court never lets things settle, while the wise hold back anger and calm things down.

parts.label: Rulers and the poor (vv. 12-14)
parts.note: When a ruler listens to lies, his officials become wicked too. The poor person and the one who exploits them both receive their sight, likely meaning their very life, from the LORD, so a king who judges the poor fairly is promised a lasting throne.

parts.label: Discipline and guidance (vv. 15-18)
parts.note: Verses 15 and 17 reflect ancient household discipline, where the rod was normal, and say correction brings a child wisdom and parents peace; verse 16 adds that sin spreads when the wicked thrive, though their fall will come. The "vision" or "revelation" in verse 18 means a message from God through prophets, not personal goals, and without it people throw off restraint.

parts.label: Servants and hasty words (vv. 19-21)
parts.note: The servants here were household slaves or workers, and the sayings claim words alone will not move them, while a person who speaks in haste is worse off than a fool. The last word of verse 21 is unclear in Hebrew, so scholars are unsure whether a pampered servant ends up insolent or acting like a son.

parts.label: Anger, pride, and true justice (vv. 22-27)
parts.note: A hot temper breeds conflict and pride brings a person low, and verse 24 likely refers to a law that put a public curse on anyone who knew of a crime and stayed silent. Fearing people is called a trap, real justice is said to come from the LORD rather than a ruler's favor, and honest and dishonest people find each other repulsive.

think: Whose correction do you find easiest to hear, and whose do you tend to brush off?
